title: helm-private-values-init-hooks: add KMS encryption + nodeSelector support and tighten init hook templating
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require more flexible node targeting and secure secrets bootstrapping for init hooks. Existing helm chart init hooks for private values assumed a single, general init pod and did not surface configuration for KMS-backed encryption of generated secret values nor nodeSelector/toleration support for air-gapped or restricted-cluster installs.

What this PR does: Adds optional KMS encryption support and nodeSelector/toleration fields to the private-values init hook templating and values schema. Changes are backwards compatible by default and guarded behind clearly named values keys. Specifically: updates values.schema.json, templates/private-values-init.yaml, and adds helper templates for kms encryption and node selection. Ensures initHook respects .Values.privateInit.nodeSelector and .Values.privateInit.tolerations, and optionally encrypts generated secrets via .Values.privateInit.kms.enabled with provider integration placeholders (KMS key ARN / key ID).

Files changed (high level): updated schema to validate new keys; refined init hook template with conditional blocks for KMS encryption; added unit tests for helm template rendering and a CI chart lint step. Includes migration notes for Dedicated/Private customers that currently rely on plaintext init hook secrets.

Upgrade / rollback considerations: Backwards compatible by default. If a customer enables kms.enabled true during an upgrade, init hook will attempt to call the configured KMS provider to encrypt generated secrets; operators must ensure the installer has network/KMS access or supply a fallback. Rollback will preserve existing secrets but documentation recommends performing a one-time rebootstrap when toggling encryption to avoid mixed-secret formats.

Testing: Local helm template render tests added; chart lint and kubeval run in CI. Verified on a k8s 1.26 test cluster in CI with both KMS disabled and a mocked KMS provider enabled. Manual validation performed for nodeSelector + toleration propagation across init job and rollout hook pods.

Related: ENG-4672 (private installer init hooks), SUP-1291 (customer reported missing node targeting).

release_notes:
- charts/redwood-private: add optional KMS encryption for private-init hook secrets (privateInit.kms).
- charts/redwood-private: expose nodeSelector and tolerations for init hook pods (privateInit.nodeSelector, privateInit.tolerations).
- helm: stricter values.schema.json validation for privateInit keys.
notes_for_ops: When enabling privateInit.kms.enabled: ensure installer/service account has permissions to call the configured KMS (KMS key ARN/ID configured in values). If cluster is air-gapped, provide a KMS proxy or leave kms.enabled=false and rotate secrets manually. For nodeSelector changes, validate that the selected nodes are schedulable for init pods.
manual_test_steps:
1) Render the chart with defaults: helm template . -f values.yaml --show-only templates/private-values-init.yaml and confirm no kms blocks rendered.
2) Enable kms: set privateInit.kms.enabled=true and provide privateInit.kms.keyId mock; render and confirm kmsEncryption block appears.
3) Set privateInit.nodeSelector and privateInit.tolerations; install to a test cluster and confirm init job pods land on expected nodes.
4) Run chart-lint and kubeval workflow to ensure schema compliance.
